answer: Time-locked vesting escrow splits each identity’s rewards into a slow release curve keyed to a rotating cipher, so a fresh identity must post a per-identity bond and wait through withdrawal latency before any payout clears. A beacon timestamp caps withdrawals per epoch, while a five-member mesa quorum must attest early release; faking N identities costs N bonds plus per-attempt fees, and a coordinated ring gains nothing because escrow stays locked until each member earns trust, making abandonment a net loss.
